newsitem.title: JAPAN: Tokyo corn futures end sharply higher on yen fall.
newsitem.headline: Tokyo corn futures end sharply higher on yen fall.

text.p: Tokyo corn futures extended their early gains to end sharply higher on Monday, as private investors' buying gathered force with support from the yen's fall against the dollar, traders said.
Prices ranged from 320 yen to 490 yen tonne higher, with the benchmark November 1997 contract up by 320 yen at 14,050 yen per tonne. Daily volume was 45,246 lots.

The market started the day on a firmer note as cautious views that the market was oversold encouraged technical buying. But they said further upside potential could be limited as the market may receive little support from the Chicago market.
The spot December contract on the CBOT Project A trading system was being traded at $2.74 per bushel at 0817 GMT, against $2.72-1/2 at Friday's close.
The spot January contract of the CBOT soybean futures on the overnight trading system was traded at $7.12 per bushel at 0818 GMT, against $7.09-1/2 at Friday's close.
